title: D2-S1 Live check: one Auto send routes, and category variants reach pools (or do not)
body:
## Goal
Confirm on the real machine that an Auto send routes end to end, and confirm or refute that category variants are silently dropped on pool categories (design section 2.4, source-derived).

## Context
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D2-categories-auto-switching.md sections 2.2, 2.4, 4.3, 5. Baseline: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/baseline/v1-decisions-auto.md (Classification flow, Live health). Source: openchamber origin/HEAD packages/web/server/lib/routing/runtime.js (withKnownVariant, resolveAutoSelection).

## Steps
1. Read the routing state (describe payload): autoReady true, jevAvailable true, classifier.effective non-null, at least 2 enabled categories.
2. Settings, Routing, Test: the classifier answers the probe with blue or table and a confidence.
3. In a scratch session in /home/user/git/code with model openchamber/auto, send three prompts from design 4.3: trivial (rename one local variable), hard (cross-module fix with unknown cause), follow-up thanks (expect held by stickiness).
4. For each send, capture the openchamber:routing.decision event payload.
5. Read the OpenCode model catalog entry for opencode-route/workhorse and opencode-route/speed: record the variants list.
6. Run route_usage for the scratch session: record which pool attempts happened.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- A result comment on this issue holds the three decision payloads, the catalog variant lists and the route_usage rows.
- Oracle per decision: category in the enabled set, and the chosen pool equals the category pool when reason is routed, else the fallback.
- Variant drop: either variantDropped is present for the pool categories (confirmed) or the variant reached the pool (refuted). Say which.
- Record ms per decision (feeds the 5 s budget question Q13).

## Oracle
The decision payload and the catalog listing (reference: the source code path, plus the live catalog).

title: D2-S2 Smoke test: one Auto send with a logged decision, runnable without a provider
body:
## Goal
A runnable smoke test: one Auto send, stubbed classifier and OpenCode, asserting one decision line with a category in the enabled set and a model equal to that category pool.

## Context
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D2-categories-auto-switching.md section 5 and 4.3. Existing injection points in createRoutingRuntime (runtime.js): readSessionHistory, readConfigEntries, listCatalogModels, and a jev stub. Existing routing tests sit beside the modules (cache.test.js, history.test.js).

## Files
- new packages/web/server/lib/routing/auto-smoke.test.js

## Approach
- Build a routing.json fixture with the five built-ins (design 4.1 mapping; use the current machine mapping as a second fixture).
- Stub jev to answer choice trivial with confidence 0.92.
- Stub the catalog so opencode-route/small lists no variants (the V1 case) and assert the variant is dropped and recorded (depends on D2-S3).
- A second case: jev throws; assert reason error and the fallback model.
- A live case guarded by env AUTO_SMOKE_LIVE=1 that calls the real classifier source; skipped by default.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- node --test packages/web/server/lib/routing/auto-smoke.test.js passes with no network.
- With AUTO_SMOKE_LIVE=1 and a usable source, the live case passes against the same oracle.

## Oracle
Invariant: category in enabled set; chosen pool equals pool(category) when reason routed, else fallback. Stub answers are the golden input.

title: D2-S3 Record every Auto decision and every dropped variant in an append-only JSONL
body:
## Goal
Every Auto send writes one append-only line to auto-decisions.jsonl in the OpenChamber data dir (mode 0600). A variant the pool does not advertise is recorded as variant_dropped, never silently dropped.

## Context
Design sections 4.4 (line schema, mapped to AD7 decision_record), 4.2 (variant rule), 3.8 (why JSONL in V2). Baseline: v1-decisions-auto.md Recording and logging today. Source: store.js path helpers (around line 180-184), runtime.js withKnownVariant.

## Files
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/store.js (path, append, size gate)
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/runtime.js (build line, withKnownVariant records variant_dropped)
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/defaults.js (none expected)

## Approach
- Mint decision_id as dec_ plus a ULID per send. Fields exactly as design 4.4 AutoDecisionLine.
- Append with fs.appendFile, create with mode 0600, reject a non-regular file (match the existing bounded-reader style).
- Keep the in-memory event unchanged; the file is additional.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- Test: two Auto sends append exactly two lines; earlier bytes are unchanged (prefix equality).
- Test: a dropped variant produces variant_dropped with requested and pool.
- Test: file mode is 0600 on create.

## Oracle
Golden line fixture for one routed send, plus the append-only invariant (prefix check). Schema from design 4.4 is the reference.

title: D2-S4 Call-time classifier failover along a chain, and fallback agent build
body:
## Goal
When the chosen classifier source fails at call time, try the next usable source inside one total budget (5 s), then the fallback model with agent build. Record which source answered.

## Context
Design sections 3.6 (order B), 3.7 (failure path B), 4.8 (flow), 6 (decision still pending Drew, Q3/Q6; implement the mechanism behind a config list so the order can change). Current code: classifier.js FALLBACK_ORDER applies at config time only (line 106-108); runtime.js resolveAccess; jev.js ask (4000 ms).

## Files
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/classifier.js (chain builder)
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/runtime.js (attempt loop, budget)
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/defaults.js (fallback.agent default build; chain default from design 3.6 B)
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/store.js (accept fallback.agent)

## Approach
- chain = [pick] + [zen-promo if ZEN_JEV_PROMOTION_ACTIVE] + [zen-key, typesafe, openrouter, vercel] filtered by usable, first occurrence kept. custom is excluded unless the config lists it (design Q4).
- attempt loop with a deadline = now + 5000 ms; each attempt uses min(4000, remaining).
- decision line gets classifier.attempt and classifier.source (S3 schema).

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- Stub jev: source 1 times out, source 2 answers: attempt 2, source 2 recorded.
- All sources fail: reason error, fallback model with agent build, total elapsed under 5.2 s (fake timers).

## Oracle
Property test: for any sequence of per-source outcomes (ok, timeout, http error, bad json), the chain stops at the first ok, never calls an unusable source, never exceeds the deadline. Reference: the pure chain function.

title: D2-S5 Built-in categories docs and ops, with criteria text
body:
## Goal
Add two built-in categories, docs and ops, with the criteria text from the design, so Jev separates prose work and infra or repo operations from implement and hard.

## Context
Design sections 3.1 (options A and B), 4.1 (criteria and the destructive-to-hard rule). Built-in list: defaults.js BUILTIN_CATEGORIES (around line 132-158). Criteria text style: keep about reasoning demanded, never reply length (the comment at the top of defaults.js).

## Files
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/defaults.js (two entries, ids docs and ops)
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/jev.js (none expected; buildRoutingRequest already maps any category)
- new fixture packages/web/server/lib/routing/fixtures/criteria.golden.json

## Approach
- Built-in docs and ops carry no model; the shipped default is the fallback pair until the user maps them (D2-S12 applies the mapping). Confirm the category model default is empty and the fallback is used.
- Keep descriptions within MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- node --test: buildRoutingRequest over the 7 built-ins matches the golden criteria.
- Each description is a single line (no CR or LF) and within MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH.

## Oracle
Golden file of the criteria object (reference: design 4.1 text). Single-line invariant (existing regex in jev.js).

title: D2-S6 Guard: decision-line invariants (property test over random decisions)
body:
## Goal
A guard that fails when a decision line breaks the invariants of design section 4.4.

## Context
Design section 4.4 Invariants: reason routed implies category in categories_enabled; chosen pool equals the category pool or the fallback; decision_id unique; the file only grows (AD7).

## Files
- new packages/web/server/lib/routing/auto-decisions.test.js

## Approach
- Generate random configs (1 to 8 categories, some disabled), random answers (known id, unknown id, low confidence, error), random sequences of 1 to 30 sends through the runtime with stubs.
- Check the invariants on the written JSONL after each sequence.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- node --test packages/web/server/lib/routing/auto-decisions.test.js passes with a fixed seed and 500 cases.
- Mutating the runtime to choose a disabled category makes the test fail (manual check recorded in the PR).

## Oracle
Invariant check (the four rules above). The generator is the input; the invariant is the oracle.

title: D2-S7 Guard: routing categories check (bin/check-routing-categories.mjs)
body:
## Goal
A check that the machine routing.json categories point at real opencode-route pools, carry only the tiers low, medium or high (or none), and that at least two categories are enabled.

## Context
Design sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.10. Precedent: bin/check-opencode-route-rules.mjs (route class guard). Operator scripts follow the strict argument contract in doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md: declare the command line in the header and reject unknown flags with a non-zero exit.

## Files
- new bin/check-routing-categories.mjs
- new bin/fixtures/routing-categories/ (valid and invalid cases)

## Approach
- Args: --routing <path> --config <path to .opencode/opencode.jsonc>. Anything else is a usage error.
- Pools come from experimental.model_routes keys in the jsonc (use the repo's existing jsonc reader if one exists; otherwise a strict JSON-with-comments strip).
- Checks: model.providerID is opencode-route; model.modelID is a key of model_routes or one of small, scout, speed, workhorse, specialist, summit; variant in low, medium, high or absent; enabled categories at least 2; no model string with a # pin.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- node bin/check-routing-categories.mjs --routing bin/fixtures/routing-categories/valid.json --config .opencode/opencode.jsonc exits 0.
- The invalid fixtures (unknown pool, variant xhigh, one enabled category) each exit non-zero with the failing rule named.
- An unknown flag exits non-zero before reading any file.

## Oracle
Golden fixtures: valid passes, each invalid case fails with its named rule.

title: D2-S8 Make Auto the OpenChamber default, with a no-loop test for a stale Auto
body:
## Goal
With Auto proven (D2-S1), make openchamber/auto the default model in OpenChamber settings, clear the /home/user/git/code project override, and prove a stale Auto never lands on Auto.

## Context
Design sections 3.4, 4.7 and 2.5. The cascade is in packages/ui/src/stores/useConfigStore.ts (resolveProviderModelSelection and dropStaleAutoSelection, around lines 320-345 and 3600). isStaleAutoSelection at line 290. Project defaults override the global one.

## Files
- packages/ui/src/stores/useConfigStore.ts (none, unless the pure helper needs exporting)
- packages/ui/src/stores/useConfigStore.test.ts (new cases)
- DOCUMENTATION for the default (packages/ui docs, if a page exists)

## Approach
- Settings UI sets defaultModel to openchamber/auto (handleModelChange clears defaultVariant).
- Set or clear the project entry; do not hand-edit settings.json while OpenChamber runs.
- Test: with routing not ready, settingsDefaultModel openchamber/auto and no project default resolves to a non-Auto model (opencode config.model).

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- The new test passes.
- After the Settings change, a new draft session in /home/user/git/code opens on openchamber/auto when routing is ready, and on the workhorse pool when it is not (manual, recorded).

## Oracle
Test oracle: the resolved selection is never openchamber/auto when autoReady is false.

title: D2-S9 Guidance: heavy parallel sub-sessions, depth, when not to use Auto, when to self-route
body:
## Goal
Put the sub-session guidance into the topic file read by every session: fan out with small contexts, sub-sessions can make sub-sessions, when not to use Auto, when to change pool, and that every routing call is recorded.

## Context
Design section 4.6, section 7 and Appendix A (the exact text). AGENTS.md is 7,493 of 8,000 bytes, so the text goes in .opencode/instructions/subagents.md. Existing file: .opencode/instructions/subagents.md (its section on model switching is the one to correct: state that a switch is possible only through pool_switch).

## Files
- .opencode/instructions/subagents.md (new section, replace the model-switching sentence)
- AGENTS.md (at most one index line under Subagent-first workflow, only if the budget allows)

## Approach
- Use Appendix A of the design verbatim, then review it with a zero-context reader (writing-for-agents skill).
- Do not add a new skill.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- python3 -I scripts/research_workflow.py check passes.
- wc -c AGENTS.md stays at or below 8000.
- A zero-context reader can state the four rules (fan out small, sub-sessions nest to depth 5, when not to use Auto, when to self-route) from the section alone.

## Oracle
Budget check (scripts/research_workflow.py check) and the zero-context read-back.

title: D2-S10 Research: is session_switch_model exposed to sessions, and do route pools advertise variants
body:
## Goal
Settle two facts the design rests on: (a) whether the session_switch_model tool (origin/HEAD packages/core/src/tool/plugin/opencode.ts 179-195) is in a fresh session's Code Mode catalog in the running build, (b) whether route pools list any variant in the model catalog.

## Context
Design Q8, Q9, section 3.5 and AD10 correction (main.md AD10). Today this session's catalog shows tools.opencode.session_move and worktree tools only.

## Steps
1. Start a fresh session in the repo worktree. Search the Code Mode catalog for session_switch_model (search with namespace opencode).
2. Read the model catalog for opencode-route/workhorse and opencode-route/speed.
3. Record the running build version.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- A result comment with the search output, the catalog variant lists, and the build version.
- If the tool is exposed, open a note that the fork guard (D2-S14) is required before any use.

## Oracle
The live catalog listing (reference: the fork source at origin/HEAD).

title: D2-S11 pool_switch: bounded suggest and subsession tool, recorded as decisions
body:
## Goal
A tool a session calls to suggest or launch a subsession on an allow-listed pool or category. Every call is validated, recorded, and never switches the caller's own model.

## Context
Design sections 4.5 (signature, validator order, pseudocode), 3.5 (option B and C), 4.4 (recording), 8.2 (worked example), main AD10. Subagent tool takes a model argument (opencode-route/<pool>#effort). Depth cap experimental.subagent_depth default 5.

## Files
- new bin/routing-pool-switch.mjs (validator, recorder, launcher adapter)
- new bin/routing-pool-switch.test.mjs
- tool exposure: a mcpx or code-mode entry per the mcpx-opencode2 skill (decide in the PR; record the path)

## Approach
- allow-list = category pools of enabled categories, union opencode-route keys of experimental.model_routes. Never openchamber/auto, never a raw provider model, never the caller's own pool (self-target).
- Limits: 3 subsession launches per parent per hour; remaining depth at least 1.
- Recording appends one AutoDecisionLine (kind self-switch) to the same JSONL as D2-S3.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- node --test bin/routing-pool-switch.test.mjs passes.
- A suggest call with an allowed target returns validator ok and writes one line; mode subsession with depth 0 returns depth-exhausted and launches nothing.

## Oracle
Property test: for any target string, validator ok if and only if the target is in the allow-list and not self, and never for openchamber/auto or a raw provider id. The allow-list (from the config) is the oracle.

title: D2-S12 Trial: apply the category mapping to the machine and measure for 14 days
body:
## Goal
Apply the design 4.1 mapping (trivial to small low, research to workhorse medium, implement to workhorse medium, review to specialist high, hard to summit high, docs to scout medium, ops to workhorse high) through Settings, and measure against the current mapping for 14 days.

## Trial record (pre-registered, AD9)
- Hypothesis: docs and ops requests stop reaching hard and implement, cutting summit and workhorse attempts per category without a success-rate drop.
- Margin: category success rate (PR merged, not reverted) at least 95 percent of baseline; cost per merged PR not higher than baseline.
- Review date: 2026-11-27 (14 days after the change).
- Revert condition: any category success rate below the margin, or route_usage shows a walled pool used more than before.
- Sample size: at least 30 routed sends per category before the review, else extend.

## Context
Design 4.1, 3.2 (variant unset until D1), 9 Q2. Apply only after D2-S1 proves the path and D2-S4 lands the failover. Use Settings, not hand edits.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- routing.json on the machine matches design 4.1 (checked by bin/check-routing-categories.mjs, D2-S7).
- The trial record is in the issue and in the routing DOCUMENTATION.

## Oracle
Decision lines (D2-S3) joined to route_usage per session; the margin and revert conditions above are the oracle.

title: D2-S13 Record the classifier provider order (pick, free, paid; Cloudflare excluded) in the routing docs
body:
## Goal
Once Drew decides design Q3 and Q6 (provider order and promo as fallback), record the ruling in the routing docs and the classifier comments, so the code and the brief agree.

## Context
Design section 3.6 (option B recommended), section 6, Q4 (Cloudflare excluded, dead by ruling opencode#1651), Q6 (promo as fallback reverses classifier.js:17-20; Dax approved terms in defaults.js:28-40). Do not start until Drew's ruling is recorded on the program issue.

## Files
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/DOCUMENTATION.md (Where a Jev request goes)
- packages/web/server/lib/routing/classifier.js (the comment above FALLBACK_ORDER, only if D2-S4 did not already rewrite it)

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- DOCUMENTATION states the chain order exactly as implemented in D2-S4.
- A grep for never a fallback in the routing package returns no stale statement.

## Oracle
The chain function (D2-S4 property test) is the reference; the docs must match it.

title: D2-S14 Fork guard: top-level self-switch of session_switch_model uses the pool allow-list
body:
## Goal
A session's own model switch (session_switch_model with the session id omitted or equal to the caller) is checked against the same allow-list as pool_switch and denied with the allowed list named. Top-level sessions are unchecked today.

## Context
Design section 4.12 and 3.5 (option D). Source: packages/core/src/tool/plugin/opencode.ts 179-195 (tool), packages/core/src/session/session.ts 137-160 (governance only when parentID or fork source is set). Gate: V3 entry (design 4.11). Blocked by the V2 tool so the allow-list exists in one place.

## Files
- packages/core/src/tool/plugin/opencode.ts
- packages/core/src/session/session.ts
- governance config tests under packages/core/test

## Approach
- Enforce the allow-list for self-switch only; children keep their existing governance.
- Denial message names the allowed models (match the existing text style).

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- A top-level self-switch to a non-allow-listed model is denied; to an allow-listed pool it is allowed.
- Existing governance tests still pass.

## Oracle
Property test over model refs: allowed iff in the allow-list. Reference: the allow-list in the config.

title: D2-S15 Research: prompt-cache hit rate around model switches (gate for in-place switching)
body:
## Goal
Measure the cache-hit rate of the first turn after a model switch, and the turns it takes to recover, so the in-place switch rule (design 4.11 V3-c) has data behind its thresholds.

## Context
Design 4.11 V3-c (pseudocode with the 5 min TTL), 6.2 and R1 section 6.2 (cache economics, marked unverified in parts). Data: opencode.db route_attempt cache tokens (baseline v1-data-sources), and the decision lines from D2-S3.

## Steps
1. From route_attempt, for sessions that switched model, compute cache-read tokens over the first three turns after each switch.
2. Compare with sessions that did not switch, same pool, same window.
3. Report medians and p90 with n for each.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- A written result with n per group, the query text, and the window used.
- Thresholds proposed for the switch rule, each with its sample size.

## Oracle
The query output (reproducible from the stored SQL in the result).

title: D2-S16 In-place switch with the cache gate (pool_switch mode switch)
body:
## Goal
Add mode switch to pool_switch: a session moves its own model in place at a turn boundary, only when the cache gate allows it.

## Context
Design 4.11 V3-c (gate pseudocode), 3.5 (option D), 4.12 (fork guard). Precedent: OpenChamber cacheHoldCategory (cache.js). Blocked by the fork guard and the measured thresholds.

## Files
- bin/routing-pool-switch.mjs (mode switch, gate)
- bin/routing-pool-switch.test.mjs

## Approach
- Gate: at turn boundary only; switch when cache is cold (idle at least 5 min) or the target shares the door; otherwise compare the per-turn gain times remaining turns against the rebuild cost.
- Thresholds come from D2-S15.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- Property test: the gate never switches mid-turn; never switches when the rebuild cost exceeds the gain (within the measured thresholds).

## Oracle
The gate function's truth table derived from the design pseudocode; the property test uses it as reference.

title: D2-S17 Research: classifier inside the D5 decision pool, and effort as a tie-break lean
body:
## Goal
Decide whether Auto's classifier moves to the D5 decision pool (AD5) and whether effort becomes a tie-break lean (supplement section 6), using decision records and the probability vector D5 provides.

## Context
Design 3.3 (options A to D), 4.11 V4, 9 Q12. Cross-component ids: the D5 decision-pool slices are not yet numbered; reconcile the blocked-by link when D5 lands (provisional, design Q10). Depends on D1 for tiers.

## Steps
1. Compare Jev answers (category and confidence) with the D5 decider on the same logged prompts.
2. Measure the agreement and the cost per decision.
3. Test a lean rule on prompts where the top two categories are within a fixed distance.

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- A written comparison with n, agreement and cost per decision, and a recommendation.

## Oracle
The logged decision lines as the labelled set, with outcomes from D6 where available.

title: D2-S18 Calibrate per-category confidence thresholds from recorded decisions
body:
## Goal
Replace the single minConfidence (0.6) with a per-category threshold derived from the measured kept-rate of routed answers, with a guard that fails on drift.

## Context
Design 4.11 V3-a. Inputs: decision lines (D2-S3), D2-S12 trial data (at least 14 days), and D6 outcome links (AD7). Gate: V3 entry.

## Files
- bin/ or packages/web routing calibration module (decide in the PR)
- a guard test that fails when a category kept-rate drops below its floor

## Acceptance (runnable checks)
- Each category threshold has n and its kept-rate curve.
- The guard fails on a fixture where a category kept-rate is below its floor.

## Oracle
The kept-rate curve on the held-out decision lines; the floor is the pre-registered margin from D2-S12.
